messages.subject: generic model
messages.body_plain:
Hi Folks,

I have tried running a model with two factors in the "generic" list. As the factor are somewhat related (additive and dominance kinship matrices), even using "em" there are problems in convergence.

Thus, I wondering define the initial values for components of variance. How could I do it?

Thanks,

messages.subject: BLUP interpretation
messages.body_plain:
Hi Folks,
We have a dataset with known mothers and some (most) known fathers. In the PBV.full results we got the number of  BLUPs which sums up to the number of mothers, fathers and all individuals. How to interpret the values we got? We suppose that BV for mothers go first, then for fathers and then for the individual trees in the test. Is that right?

Jan Kowalczyk
Daniel Chmura

messages.subject: Re: [breedR] generic model
messages.body_plain:
Dear Roberto,

See the argument |var.ini| of |remlf90()| in the help (|?remlf90|).

Here is a reproducible example with a valid specification of the initial
variances within the generic components:

|# Dummy fit: just to retrieve incidence and covariance matrices rdummy
<- remlf90( fixed = phe_X ~ 1, genetic = list( model = 'add_animal',
pedigree = globulus[, 1:3], id = 'self', var.ini = 10 ), spatial = list(
model = 'blocks', coord = globulus[, c('x','y')], id = 'bl', var.ini = 1
), var.ini = list(resid = 5), data = globulus ) # Same model with
generic components res <- remlf90( fixed = phe_X ~ 1, generic = list( ##
genetic add = with( rdummy$effects$genetic$effects$direct,
list(incidence.matrix, structure.matrix, var.ini = 10) ), ## spatial bl
= with( rdummy$effects$spatial$effects$blocks, list(incidence.matrix,
structure.matrix, var.ini = 1) ) ), var.ini = list(resid = 5), data =
globulus ) |

Best wishes

ƒacu.-

Sorry, the code went unreadable. Here it goes again.

# Dummy fit: just to retrieve incidence and covariance matrices
rdummy <- remlf90(
  fixed   = phe_X ~ 1,
  genetic = list(
    model    = 'add_animal',
    pedigree = globulus[, 1:3],
    id       = 'self',
    var.ini = 10
  ),
  spatial = list(
    model = 'blocks',
    coord = globulus[, c('x','y')],
    id    = 'bl',
    var.ini = 1
  ),
  var.ini = list(resid = 5),
  data    = globulus
)

# Same model with generic components
res <- remlf90(
  fixed  = phe_X ~ 1,
  generic = list(
    ## genetic
    add = with(
      rdummy$effects$genetic$effects$direct,
      list(incidence.matrix, structure.matrix, var.ini = 10)
    ),
    ## spatial
    bl = with(
      rdummy$effects$spatial$effects$blocks,
      list(incidence.matrix, structure.matrix, var.ini = 1)
    )
  ),
  var.ini = list(resid = 5),
  data   = globulus
)

messages.subject: Re: [breedR] BLUP interpretation
messages.body_plain:
Dear Jan and Daniel,

The order of the result depends on the original coding scheme, and whether there has been need of recodification or not.

Here is a toy example with 15 individuals in total (only 5 observed), with random codes where you recover the BVs in the original codification. It is completely general and works under any circumstances.

set.seed(123); n.ped <- 5
ped.nightmare <- matrix(sample(30, n.ped*3), n.ped, 3,
                        dimnames = list(NULL, c('self', 'sire', 'dam')))

## Obviously, the pedigree is recoded
ped <- build_pedigree(1:3, data = ped.nightmare)
#> Warning in build_pedigree(1:3, data = ped.nightmare): The pedigree has been
#> recoded. Check attr(ped, 'map').

## Simulated data
(dat <- data.frame(
  ped.nightmare,
  y = rnorm(n.ped)
))
#>   self sire dam          y
#> 1    9    2  20  1.2805549
#> 2   23   13  30 -1.7272706
#> 3   12   21  22  1.6901844
#> 4   24   27  29  0.5038124
#> 5   25   10  26  2.5283366

## Fitted model
res <- remlf90(
  fixed = y ~ 1,
  genetic = list(
    model    = 'add_animal',
    pedigree = ped,
    id       = 'self'
  ),
  data = dat
)
#> No specification of initial variances.
#>      Using default value of 1 for all variance components.
#>      See ?breedR.getOption.

## BV in internal codes (sorted, consecutive, from 1 to 15)
BV <- ranef(res)$genetic

## Get the BLUPs for all 15 individuals in the original codes
## use the "map" attribute of the recoded pedigree
data.frame(
  BV = BV[attr(ped, "map")]
)[!is.na <http://is.na>(attr(ped, "map")),, drop = FALSE]
#>             BV
#> 2   0.10618394
#> 9   0.21236787
#> 10  0.41761928
#> 12  0.41684771
#> 13 -0.64454290
#> 20  0.10618394
#> 21  0.20842385
#> 22  0.20842385
#> 23 -1.28908580
#> 24 -0.17536833
#> 25  0.83523855
#> 26  0.41761928
#> 27 -0.08768416
#> 29 -0.08768416
#> 30 -0.64454290

Hope it helps!
    ƒacu.-
